questions.stem:
"Antibiotic resistance arises when bacteria acquire genetic changes — by mutation or horizontal gene transfer — that reduce susceptibility to a drug. Resistant strains survive treatment and proliferate, so each course of antibiotics applies selective pressure favouring resistance. Resistance spreads faster in populations with high antibiotic use."

Which is the best-supported conclusion?
options: Antibiotic use creates genetic mutations directly.
Resistance cannot arise without horizontal gene transfer.
Reducing unnecessary antibiotic use would slow the spread of resistance.
All bacteria become resistant after one course.
Resistance is independent of selection pressure.
questions.exp: If use applies selection favouring resistance, lowering use reduces that pressure. A misstates mutation origin; B and D are absolute/false; E contradicts the passage.

questions.stem:
"Homeostasis refers to the maintenance of a constant internal environment despite external changes. Core variables such as body temperature, blood pH, and blood glucose are regulated by negative feedback loops: a sensor detects deviation, a control centre orchestrates a response, and an effector returns the variable to its set point."

Which is consistent with the passage?
options: A positive-feedback loop is the main homeostatic mechanism.
The effector's job is to push the variable further from the set point.
Negative feedback returns a variable toward its set point.
Body temperature is not a homeostatically regulated variable.
questions.exp: Negative feedback returns the variable to set point.

questions.stem: (General knowledge) The Italian Renaissance anatomist who published De humani corporis fabrica (1543), correcting many Galenic errors through direct dissection, was:
questions.exp: Vesalius's Fabrica is a foundation of modern anatomy. (Note: Harvey — blood circulation — was English.)

questions.stem: Four students — P, Q, R, S — are ranked in an exam. P scored higher than Q but lower than R. S scored lower than Q. Who scored lowest?
questions.exp: Order from high to low: R > P > Q > S. Lowest = S.

questions.stem: "If it rains, the match is cancelled." The match was not cancelled. Therefore:
questions.exp: Modus tollens on (Rain → Cancelled); ¬Cancelled ⇒ ¬Rain.

questions.stem: A machine applies the rule: take a number, square it, then subtract 4. If the output is 32, the input could be:
At 9:45, what is the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock?
A is the father of B. B is the sister of C. How is A related to C?
questions.exp: B and C are siblings sharing father A.

questions.stem: Complete the series: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ?
questions.exp: Perfect squares: 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², 6² = 36.

questions.stem: Glycolysis occurs in the:
questions.exp: Glycolysis is cytosolic.

questions.stem: Under anaerobic conditions in human muscle, pyruvate is converted to:
questions.exp: Lactic acid fermentation regenerates NAD⁺ so glycolysis can continue.

questions.stem: The net reaction of aerobic respiration (per glucose) produces approximately how many ATP in eukaryotes (modern estimate)?
questions.exp: Modern estimates: ~30–32 ATP/glucose in eukaryotes (older texts cite 36–38).

questions.stem: Which coenzyme carries electrons from glycolysis and the Krebs cycle to the electron transport chain?
questions.exp: NADH and FADH₂ deliver electrons to complexes I and II respectively.

questions.stem: The proton-motive force across the inner mitochondrial membrane is generated by:
options: Pumping of H⁺ from matrix to intermembrane space by electron transport complexes
questions.exp: Complexes I, III, IV pump H⁺, storing energy as an electrochemical gradient.

questions.stem: Which metabolic pathway occurs in both cellular respiration and photosynthesis?
options: Glycolysis-like reactions of the Calvin cycle only
questions.exp: Both processes use an electron transport chain coupled to chemiosmotic ATP synthesis.

questions.stem: In which organelle does photosynthesis take place in plant cells?
questions.exp: Chloroplasts contain thylakoids (light reactions) and stroma (Calvin cycle).

questions.stem: The light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis produce:
questions.exp: Light energy splits water (releasing O₂) and drives ATP + NADPH synthesis.

questions.stem: Which blood vessels carry oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
questions.exp: Pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood to the left atrium. (Note: pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood — an exception to the usual pattern.)

questions.stem: Gas exchange in the lungs occurs across the walls of the:
questions.exp: Alveoli have thin walls + large surface area for O₂/CO₂ diffusion.

questions.stem: Which cells of the gastric glands secrete hydrochloric acid?
questions.exp: Parietal cells secrete HCl and intrinsic factor.

questions.stem: Bile, which emulsifies fats, is produced by the __ and stored in the __.
questions.exp: Bile is made in the liver and concentrated/stored in the gallbladder.

questions.stem: The basic functional unit of the kidney is the:
questions.exp: Each kidney has ~1 million nephrons performing filtration, reabsorption, secretion.

questions.stem: Filtration of blood in the nephron occurs at the:
questions.exp: The glomerulus filters plasma into Bowman's capsule.

questions.stem: Which tissue lines the inner surface of the stomach and intestines?
questions.exp: Simple columnar epithelium with microvilli lines the GI tract for absorption.

questions.stem: Smooth muscle is found in the walls of all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Skeletal attachments to bone (tendons are connective tissue, not muscle)
questions.exp: Tendons are connective tissue; smooth muscle is involuntary and lines hollow organs/vessels. (Skeletal muscle attaches to bone via tendons.)

questions.stem: Which connective tissue cell type produces the fibres of regular dense connective tissue (e.g., tendons)?
questions.exp: Fibroblasts secrete collagen fibres.

questions.stem: The primary stimulus for ventilation during moderate exercise is the rise in:
options: Blood CO₂ (and H⁺), sensed by central and peripheral chemoreceptors
questions.exp: CO₂ (via H⁺) is the main driver of ventilation under most conditions.

questions.stem: Insulin promotes which of the following in liver and muscle?
questions.exp: Insulin drives glucose uptake (GLUT4) and glycogenesis.

questions.stem: The long bone of the thigh is the:
questions.exp: Femur = thigh bone (longest bone in the body).

questions.stem: A red blood cell placed in a hypertonic solution will:
questions.exp: Water leaves the cell by osmosis → crenation.

questions.stem: The phase of mitosis in which chromosomes align at the cell's equator is:
questions.exp: Chromosomes line up at the metaphase plate.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct base-pairing rule in DNA?
options: A – U and G – C (this is DNA–RNA, not DNA–DNA)
questions.exp: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine, guanine with cytosine.

questions.stem: Balance: __ Al + __ O₂ → __ Al₂O₃. The coefficient of O₂ is:
questions.exp: 4 Al + 3 O₂ → 2 Al₂O₃.

questions.stem: What is the oxidation number of Mn in KMnO₄?
25.0 mL of 0.10 M HCl is neutralised by 0.05 M NaOH. What volume of NaOH is required?
questions.exp: Moles HCl = 0.025 × 0.10 = 0.0025 mol. Need equal moles OH⁻: V = 0.0025 / 0.05 = 0.050 L = 50 mL.

questions.stem: A buffer solution resists changes in pH when small amounts of acid or base are added. A typical buffer consists of:
options: A strong acid and its conjugate base
A weak acid and its conjugate base (or weak base and its conjugate acid)
A strong acid and a strong base
questions.exp: Weak acid/conjugate base pairs (e.g., acetic acid/acetate) resist pH change.

questions.stem: Which has the highest electronegativity?
questions.exp: Fluorine is the most electronegative element (4.0 on Pauling scale).

questions.stem: The shape of a methane (CH₄) molecule is:
questions.exp: Four bonding pairs, no lone pairs → tetrahedral, 109.5°.

questions.stem: At STP, what volume is occupied by 1 mole of an ideal gas? (Use standard value.)
questions.exp: 1 mol ideal gas at STP (0 °C, 1 atm) = 22.4 L.

questions.stem: Calculate the molar mass of CaCO₃. (Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16.)
Which has the lowest pH?
questions.exp: 0.1 M HCl → pH 1 (lowest, most acidic among options).

questions.stem: Which of the following is an aromatic compound?
questions.exp: Benzene (C₆H₆) is the archetypal aromatic compound.

questions.stem: Which functional group is present in aldehydes?
questions.exp: Aldehydes have the –CHO group (carbonyl with at least one H).

questions.stem: For the equilibrium 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), ΔH < 0. Increasing temperature will:
options: Shift the equilibrium to the right
Shift the equilibrium to the left (favours endothermic direction)
questions.exp: Forward reaction is exothermic; raising T favours the reverse (endothermic) direction.

questions.stem: The isotope ¹⁴C has how many neutrons? (C atomic number = 6.)
questions.exp: Neutrons = mass number − protons = 14 − 6 = 8.

questions.stem: A catalyst increases the rate of a reaction by:
options: Providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy
Being consumed in the net reaction
questions.exp: Catalysts lower Eₐ (alternate pathway); they are regenerated and do not change K_eq.

questions.stem: What type of reaction is: CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl (in light)?
questions.exp: A H atom of methane is substituted by Cl — free-radical substitution.
Product zero ⇒ either factor zero.

questions.stem: Solve: x² − 5x + 6 = 0.
Solve the inequality: −2x + 1 > 7.
questions.exp: −2x > 6 ⇒ divide by −2 and flip: x < −3.

questions.stem: In a right triangle with legs 6 and 8, what is the hypotenuse?
A is the set {1, 2, 3}; B is the set {a, b}. How many ordered pairs are in A × B (the Cartesian product)?
A body accelerates uniformly from rest at 2 m/s² for 5 s. What distance does it cover?
Two resistors, 4 Ω and 6 Ω, are in series across a 10 V battery. What is the current?
questions.exp: R_total = 10 Ω; I = V/R = 10/10 = 1 A.

questions.stem: A 1.5 V cell delivers 0.3 A through a lamp. What is the lamp's resistance?
A 2 kg block is pushed with a force of 10 N on a frictionless surface. What is its acceleration?
A 5 kg object is lifted 2 m. How much gravitational PE is gained? (g = 9.8 m/s².)
The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is about 1/6 of that on Earth. An astronaut's weight on the Moon compared to Earth is:
questions.exp: W = mg; with g_Moon = g_Earth/6, weight is 1/6 as great.
